items.title: Implement authentication for all web API endpoints
acceptance_criteria: All /chat, /api/youtube/*, /obsidian, /notes endpoints require X-API-Key header or equivalent auth
Unauthorized requests return 401 with generic error message
API key validation uses environment variable API_KEY or similar
Integration tests pass for both authenticated and unauthenticated requests
items.approach: Create src/hooks.server.ts with auth middleware that intercepts all protected routes. Extract API key from environment. Validate on every request before handler execution.

items.title: Fix arbitrary file write vulnerability in /notes endpoint
acceptance_criteria: Filename is sanitized using basename() to prevent path traversal
Filename format validated against /^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/ pattern
Content size limited to 1MB
Resolved path verified to be within intended inbox directory
Unit tests pass for path traversal attempts (../, ../../, etc.)
items.approach: Add input validation before writeFile: sanitize with basename(), validate regex, check size, verify resolved path. Use path.resolve() to detect escapes.

items.title: Replace shell execution with Node.js APIs in /obsidian endpoint
acceptance_criteria: No execAsync or shell command execution remains
File operations use fs/promises (writeFile, mkdir, etc.)
noteName sanitized with basename() and regex validation
Content size validated (max 10MB)
Path traversal tests pass
Integration tests pass with Obsidian vault simulation
items.approach: Replace all exec() calls with Node.js fs APIs. Sanitize noteName using basename and regex. Use path.resolve() to validate final path.

items.title: Verify and enforce API key middleware on Go backend routes
acceptance_criteria: APIKeyMiddleware applied to all /api/* routes
Middleware validation enforced before handler execution
/swagger/* routes exempted from auth
Tests verify 401 response for missing/invalid API key
Documentation lists which routes require authentication
items.approach: In serve.go (or server initialization), create protected route group with middleware applied. Verify middleware is called on all sensitive handlers.

items.title: Secure GitHub token handling and prevent exposure
acceptance_criteria: .env files never created or stored with credentials
Token loaded exclusively from GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable
Token value never logged, printed, or returned in responses
Helper function MaskToken() masks tokens for logging (show first 4 + last 4 chars)
Documentation recommends token rotation and minimal scopes
items.approach: Remove .env file loading for credentials. Use environment variables only. Add MaskToken() helper. Audit all log statements for token leaks. Add logging validation tests.

items.title: Enforce HTTPS for backend API calls in production
acceptance_criteria: FABRIC_API_URL loaded from environment variable (default: http://localhost:8080 for dev)
Production builds enforce HTTPS URL validation
Error thrown if production mode and URL is not https://
Configuration documented in README or .env.example
items.approach: Add FABRIC_API_URL to environment.ts. Fetch uses environment variable. Add validation check in +server.ts for production.

items.title: Add CSRF protection and server-side session validation
acceptance_criteria: CSRF token generated and included in meta tag on every page
Session API calls include X-CSRF-Token header
Backend validates CSRF token on all session endpoints
Sessions tied to authenticated user, not just session name
Users can only access their own sessions (server-side validation)
items.approach: Enable SvelteKit CSRF protection. Generate token in hooks. Include in session API calls. Backend validates before returning session data.

items.title: Add input validation on chat and pattern endpoints
acceptance_criteria: Request size validated (max 2MB)
userInput length capped (max 10000 chars)
patternName validated against /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ pattern
Message array length limited (max 100 messages)
Null bytes rejected in inputs
Unit tests verify validation rejections
items.approach: Add validation checks before JSON parsing and before forwarding to backend. Return 400 Bad Request with generic message for invalid input.

items.title: Restrict file permissions on session files
acceptance_criteria: Session files saved with 0600 permissions (owner read/write only)
Session directory created with 0700 permissions
os.Chmod() called after file creation to enforce permissions
Integration test verifies file permissions are correctly set
items.approach: After SaveAsJson, call os.Chmod(sessionFilePath, 0600). Create helper EnsureSessionDirPermissions(0700). Call during initialization.

items.title: Implement rate limiting on API endpoints
acceptance_criteria: Rate limit: 10 requests per minute per IP (configurable)
429 Too Many Requests returned when limit exceeded
Retry-After header included in 429 responses
Different limits for different endpoints (e.g., chat: 10/min, youtube: 5/min)
Integration tests verify rate limit enforcement
items.approach: Create rateLimiter.ts with Upstash or in-memory limit store. Apply in hooks.server.ts middleware. Key by client IP. Return 429 when exceeded.

items.title: Sanitize error messages in production
acceptance_criteria: Detailed error messages only returned when NODE_ENV === 'development'
Production returns generic 'An error occurred processing your request'
Detailed errors logged server-side for debugging
No stack traces, file paths, or API details in client responses
All error paths tested in both dev and prod modes
items.approach: Wrap all catch blocks with isDevelopment check. Log detailed error. Return generic message to client.

items.title: Create abstraction layer for web routes to AI providers
acceptance_criteria: AIFacade class created with methods: executePattern(), getTranscript(), etc.
All route handlers call AIFacade instead of provider implementations
Provider selection configurable (environment variable)
Fallback provider logic centralized in facade
Tests verify facade can swap providers without code changes
items.approach: Create AIFacade service class that routes depend on. Facade instantiates providers based on config. Routes call facade methods.

items.title: Reorganize changelog generator into distinct packages
acceptance_criteria: Clear package boundaries: vcs, github, generator, cache, config
Each package has a single responsibility
Minimal cross-package dependencies
Public interfaces defined, internal implementation hidden
Tests organized per package
items.approach: Refactor into: internal/vcs (git operations), internal/github (GitHub API), internal/generator (generation logic), internal/cache (persistence), internal/config (settings). Update imports.

items.title: Document authentication model and unify auth patterns
acceptance_criteria: SECURITY.md documents CLI auth (env vars), web auth (API key header)
README includes setup instructions for API key configuration
All protected endpoints listed with auth requirements
Examples show how to set API key in curl, TypeScript, etc.
items.approach: Write security documentation explaining authentication design. Create .env.example with required variables. Update README with setup.

items.title: Create API client abstraction layer for web services
acceptance_criteria: APIClient class centralizes all endpoint URLs
Service classes depend on APIClient, not hardcoded paths
Endpoint configuration loaded from environment
API versioning supported (e.g., /api/v1/, /api/v2/)
Tests verify services use APIClient correctly
items.approach: Create APIClient with methods for each endpoint type. Update ChatService and others to use APIClient. Move hardcoded URLs to configuration.

items.title: Extract business logic into service layer
acceptance_criteria: ChatSessionService manages session lifecycle
MessageProcessingService handles message validation/enrichment
Components only handle UI rendering and event delegation
Business logic fully testable without DOM
Services have clear, documented interfaces
items.approach: Create ChatSessionService and MessageProcessingService. Move session/message logic from components. Update components to call services.

items.title: Centralize configuration management
acceptance_criteria: Single configuration entry point for web app
Environment variables documented with defaults
.env.example created with all required variables
Configuration validated on startup
All hardcoded URLs/values moved to config
items.approach: Create web/src/lib/config/index.ts exporting Config object. Load from env. Update all services to import from config. Create docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

items.title: Standardize error handling and logging in Go modules
acceptance_criteria: All packages use internal/log for logging
Errors wrapped with context using fmt.Errorf(...%w...)
No panics in library code (only in main)
Structured logging used for errors
Handler middleware adds request/response logging
items.approach: Audit all error handling. Replace fmt.Println with logging calls. Wrap errors with context. Add middleware for handler logging.

items.title: Ensure AI provider instantiation uses plugin registry
acceptance_criteria: All provider instantiation goes through plugin_registry
Registry configuration-driven (file or env vars)
New providers can be added without modifying entry points
Tests verify all providers load correctly from registry
items.approach: Ensure plugin_registry is the sole factory for providers. Document how to register new providers.

items.title: Add persistence abstraction layer for file operations
acceptance_criteria: NoteRepository interface for file operations
ObsidianVaultAdapter implements vault-specific logic
Routes depend on repository abstraction, not direct file I/O
Easy to swap with database backend in future
Tests mock repository for unit testing routes
items.approach: Create NoteRepository with save/load/delete methods. Create ObsidianVaultAdapter wrapping file operations. Routes call repository.

items.title: Verify and document dependency graph to prevent circular imports
acceptance_criteria: Dependency graph generated and verified acyclic
ARCHITECTURE.md documents intended import directions
Circular import tests added to CI
No import cycles detected on build
items.approach: Use go vet or graphviz to verify no cycles. Document in ARCHITECTURE.md. Add go vet to CI.

dependencies.reason: Cannot properly test file write validation until auth prevents unauthorized access
Cannot test shell injection fixes until endpoint is protected from unauthenticated access
CSRF protection requires authenticated users; auth must be in place first
Input validation testing easier after auth layer established
Rate limiting enforces quotas per authenticated user/API key
Documentation of auth model requires auth implementation to be complete
Security documentation must cover both CLI and Go backend auth
Repository abstraction built after fixing immediate file vulnerabilities
Repository abstraction supersedes shell execution fixes
API client abstraction needed before AI provider facade can be effective
Plugin registry verification requires AI facade abstraction in place

dedup_summary: Merged F-d1a8e2f6 (unauthenticated endpoints) with F-4db5d358 (inconsistent auth patterns) into single auth implementation task. Deduplication addressed overlapping findings on input validation (F-73bb561e reuses patterns from F-5e7ef160 and F-deb91026). Error message sanitization (F-d9127866) and logging standardization (F-bec044cf) handled as separate concerns but coordinated. Architecture findings (F-c7786f89, F-cea458fb, F-5aa62f1e, F-12a57dae) ordered by dependencies rather than merged.
summary: 21 remediation items across 4 execution levels. Level 0 (10 items): Critical auth and secrets fixes, 3 days. Level 1 (6 items): Input validation, CSRF, rate limiting, 2 days. Level 2 (3 items): File security and abstraction layers, 2 days. Level 3 (2 items): Major refactoring (changelog reorganization, service extraction), 3 days. Total estimated effort: 10 days for team of 2 engineers. No items deferred; all critical security and architectural issues addressed.
